faint.description:
USE: Page and screen background. The outermost, lightest surface layer.
NOT: Not for cards or panels — those use background/surface/subtle or muted.
PAIR: text/surface/bold for all text on this surface.
EXAMPLE: App shell background, full-page layout fill.
Light → neutral/50 · Dark → neutral/950

disabled.description:
USE: Disabled surface fill. Background of any non-interactive component in disabled state.
NOT: Never use opacity to fake disabled — it breaks layered components. Use this token.
PAIR: text/surface/faint for the disabled label.
EXAMPLE: Disabled input background, disabled card fill, disabled button surface.
Light → neutral/100 · Dark → neutral/800

subtle.description:
USE: Default component surface. Cards, panels, sheets, and containers at rest.
NOT: Not for the page background (use faint) or elevated overlays (use muted).
PAIR: border/surface/subtle for card borders, text/surface/bold for headings.
EXAMPLE: Card background, sidebar panel, settings section container.
Light → neutral/100 · Dark → neutral/900

hover.description:
USE: Neutral hover fill. Applied on pointer-enter over any non-brand interactive surface.
NOT: Not a resting state. Apply only on hover. Not for brand elements — use brand hover.
PAIR: background/surface/faint as the resting surface beneath.
EXAMPLE: List row hover, menu item hover, table row hover.
Light → neutral/100 · Dark → neutral/800

pressed.description:
USE: Neutral pressed fill. Applied during pointer-down on non-brand interactive surfaces.
NOT: Not a resting or hover state. Only during active pointer-down.
PAIR: background/surface/subtle/hover as the preceding hover state.
EXAMPLE: List row pressed, menu item active, ghost button pressed.
Light → neutral/200 · Dark → neutral/700

USE: Neutral persistent selection fill. Chosen item in a non-brand context.
NOT: Not for brand-selected items — use background/brand/subtle/selected.
PAIR: border/surface/bold for the selected outline.
EXAMPLE: Selected row in a neutral list, checked item in a menu.

NOT: Not for the surface card background — use subtle. Not for inputs — use bold.
